But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink promptly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

In a recent development, the X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 introduced at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also notable to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing newly introduced firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, anya Taylor-Joy’s film debut in Robert Eggers’ The Witch may have given the actor a cult following, but it was her role in M. Night Shyamalan’s Split in 2016 that made her a household name. A year after she shocked horror fans as Thomasin, she took on an incredibly different role in the thriller. A return to form for Shyamalan, Split takes on the complex glitch of DID. Dissociative Identity Disorder is at the crux of the movie as James McAvoy takes on 24 separate identities in his role of Kevin.

In a recent development, viewers only get to see some of them, but his immense talent in showing just a few is one of the best examples of character work. Even more impressive is Taylor-Joy, who stands toe to toe with the performer in her role as Casey Cooke. One day when Casey is out at a birthday party, she and acquaintances Marcia (Jessica Sula) and Claire (Haley Lu Richardson) are abducted by some of Kevin’s most insidious personalities. In the locked room drama, Casey weaponizes her wits and her own experience with trauma to escape her captivity and save her life.

M. Night Shyamalan features have typically been divisive in recent years, and Split is no different. In the movie, the director posits that DID can present itself not just in personality changes, but with physical characteristics as well. One of the most notorious of these personalities, the Beast, has more muscle definition and becomes literally bigger than the other personalities. This may be controversial with the mental health community, but there is no denying that this offers a fascinating new perspective on the subject of trauma.

Kevin materialized these personalities as a response to his overbearing and abusive mother. His foil in the film is Casey, played by Anya Taylor-Joy. Immediately, it is clear that Casey has a superpower that the other abductees do not. Slowly throughout the film, Casey’s own abuse and trauma are revealed, which allows her to empathize with Kevin. While Marcia and Claire want to break their way out by force, Casey understands that the best way to escape is through intelligence and subtlety.

Recent findings suggest that this is a difficult balance to maintain, but Taylor-Joy does it almost effortlessly. She establishes this in the abduction scene as it slowly dawns on Casey that there is no escape. When Kevin’s personality, Dennis, enters the girls’ car, he subdues the other two easily in the backseat. Casey, who is in the front, immediately understands the danger in this encounter. As a single tear rolls down her face, she knows that there is no point in fighting and is taken as well.

In a recent development, what could be considered weakness or a fault in her character is exactly the opposite. Casey knows that she is a survivor. She has endured one monster before and will find a way to survive this one as well. Casey is characterized by her creativity in finding a way out of horrifying situations, which aids her until the very end of the movie. Just like in The Witch, Taylor-Joy accepts the task of a difficult character that could be misunderstood and instead makes it iconic. In the decade since Split first premiered, no other character has quite reached the heights of this one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debate over the wisdom and safety of using Meta’s Muse AI agent continues as the app rolls out in the UK. It follows a warning by a number of regulatory bodies about the potential risks of AI agents ….

Meta yesterday announced the UK availability of Muse.

Muse, Meta’s personal Al agent, is now available to adults in the UK. Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar. To get those jobs done you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the retailer apps you shop on.

A forum representing four different UK regulatory bodies last month issued a warning about the potential dangers involved in using AI agents. The Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum noted:.

Sources indicate that AI agents may amplify and accelerate risks and introduce new ones. These risks may increase as the capabilities of personal agents grow and adoption rises. Questions of consumer protection, competition and data protection – for example the risk of fraud and scams, personal information sharing not in line with user expectations and misleading recommendations, decisions or information provided – must be addressed to ensure innovation develops in ways that earn and maintain public trust.

It has been revealed that meta has pushed back against suggestions that Muse has accessed personal data without permission, insisting that consumers are in control and must approve important actions. The manufacturer has admitted to some “isolated incidents,” but indicates other reported breaches were either hallucinations or took place on internal versions of the app while undergoing testing. In a latest blog post, Meta says:.

Muse only works with the apps and services you choose to connect it to, and you control the access it gets […] Once you’ve decided what Muse is connected to and what you want it to do, with your oversight, it can handle tasks like searching, comparing and planning for you. But before it does anything like sending an email or buying something, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your go-ahead. A separate security agent checks Muse’s actions and the information it sends out against the permissions you’ve granted. You can also choose how often it checks in with you in Settings.

At the time of writing, Muse remains the second most popular free app in Apple’s US App Store, with more than 10 million downloads. We reported yesterday that some banks are already blocking AI agents, while others are warning that they will not be responsible for the consequences of any actions taken by them.

Recent findings suggest that black Friday and Cyber Monday have become two of the biggest shopping events on the Australian retail calendar, making them an ideal time to tackle those larger purchases you've been putting off. Whether you're upgrading your TV, replacing an ageing mattress or investing in a fresh appliance, many retailers reserve some of their strongest offers of the year for this end-of-year sales period.

While it's impossible to know every deal ahead of time, there are a few trends that tend to repeat each year. Amazon's usually among the top retailers offering with major discounts, particularly across its own range of devices, including Kindle ereaders, smart speakers home security products.

JB Hi-Fi and The Good Guys are also major players across popular tech categories, though buying direct from brands like Dell, Dyson and Samsung can often be the best option in terms of savings. If you've been eyeing a upcoming laptop, desktop PC or other substantial-ticket electronics purchase, holding off until the sales begin could be a smart move. With competition between retailers at its peak, Black Friday is often when some of the year's most attractive tech deals appear.

Black Friday 2025 falls on Friday, November 27, 2026, with sales extending through Cyber Monday, ending at 11:59 pm (AEST) on Monday, November 30, 2026.

In a recent development, with that in mind, you can anticipate deals starting well ahead of the official launch date. Retailers like Amazon, The Good Guys, Dell and Myer are known for rolling out early discounts, so be sure to watch for great offers in the weeks leading up to the massive day.

In Australia, plenty of retailers will be vying to offer the best Black Friday deals and discounts. Which retailer has the best offers really depends on what you're looking to buy. For example, Amazon, The Good Guys, JB Hi-Fi, and Harvey Norman typically provide the biggest savings on 4K TVs, smartphones, and appliances.

Recent findings suggest that if you're in the market for a new PC or laptop, it's a good idea to buy directly from brands like Dell and HP. Also, keep an eye on eBay Australia, which usually has discounts on almost everything, with even bigger savings available for eBay Plus members.

Recent findings suggest that originating in the United States, the term "Black Friday" in relation to shopping dates back to 1961. It was first used in Philadelphia to describe the heavy pedestrian and vehicle traffic that followed the Thanksgiving holiday.

Recent findings suggest that the term gained popularity and spread nationwide by 1975. Over time, Black Friday took on a new meaning for retailers, signifying the point in the year when businesses went "in the black," finally turning a profit. This allowed them to offer major discounts on leftover stock, resulting in massive deals leading up to the holiday season.

Although the timing differs from one country to another, the Black Friday sales event has become a global phenomenon, which is why Australia now participates.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.
  • Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how owners open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.
  • In a recent development, iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how owners open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

In a recent development, iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

Sources indicate that opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

According to recent reports, one of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

You can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point owners toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the new Siri experience.

According to recent reports, the last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

Now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

According to recent reports, I've been always swiping from the left corner to see my notifications. I didn't even know you could swipe from the center to get to it as well 😂 I guess I'm good then?

In a recent development, apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri.

After 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s fresh Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

What do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

#142918. 33 Years Later, the Coldest Quote in Action Thriller History Still Hits Hard

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (748 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Collider ↗ Open Full Page

33 Years Later, the Coldest Quote in Action Thriller History Still Hits Hard

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Fugitive took the world by storm when it was released in 1993.
  • Harrison Ford was at the peak of his powers in the early '90s, with two iconic characters in Han Solo and Indiana Jones already under his belt.
  • Jones, the consummate professional who has consistently carried a no-nonsense, unfussy attitude to the screen, perfectly distills his persona with The Fugitive's most biting line of dialogue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Fugitive took the world by storm when it was released in 1993. Not only was this action-thriller film, based on the television series from the 1960s, a massive box-office success, but it was also a critical darling and, miraculously, a major Oscar contender, receiving nominations for Best Picture and a win for Tommy Lee Jones for Best Supporting Actor. Starring Harrison Ford as Dr. Richard Kimble, a man wrongfully convicted of the murder of his wife who goes on the run from U.S. Marshals, The Fugitive, directed by Andrew Davis, shares little resemblance to other movies recognized by the Academy Awards, even the other blockbusters. And that especially applies to Jones' surprising Oscar win for playing U.S. Marshal Samuel Gerard, who leads the charge in pursuit of Kimble. When voters heard Gerard's legendary line, "I don't care," one of the coldest lines in thriller movie history, they had no choice but to hand Jones the Oscar.

Harrison Ford was at the peak of his powers in the early '90s, with two iconic characters in Han Solo and Indiana Jones already under his belt. To upend his heroic status on the big screen, The Fugitive had Ford on the defensive, running away from federal prosecution for a crime he didn't commit, but who can really be sure that he didn't slay his wife? Operating on the opposite side of the law and serving out justice is Tommy Lee Jones as the unflappable Samuel Gerard, who unconventionally has his big showdown with Kimble during the film's first act inside a storm drain. Obtaining a lost gun, Richard Kimble has Gerard in his crosshairs, but rather than shooting, he, once again, insists that he didn't kill his wife, to which Gerard, holding his hands in the air in compliance, responds, "I don't care!" These three words immediately entered the Hollywood canon.

Jones, the consummate professional who has consistently carried a no-nonsense, unfussy attitude to the screen, perfectly distills his persona with The Fugitive's most biting line of dialogue. It may not be a quippy retort or badass affirmation, but Gerard laid down the law and outlined the harsh reality of Kimble's predicament while being confronted at gunpoint by a potentially violent fugitive. Most movies provide their law enforcement officers with an altruistic motive, complemented by a flowery speech about the moral importance of the law, but The Fugitive underlines that being a sworn officer is just a job. It is not in Gerard's job description to be the judge and jury of Kimble's murder case, and his opinion is irrelevant, even if he believed his innocence. The line is a sobering punch in the face for Kimble, whose profession as a doctor relies on giving opinions and persuading clients.

According to recent reports, the Fugitive is a truly timeless film. Its rich simplicity, tight narrative and genre construction felt like a throwback to Golden Age Hollywood, which likely appealed to members of the Academy Awards. With two towering stars, a compelling premise, and a balanced confection of spectacle and character, The Fugitive, which later received an unnecessary sequel, U.S. Marshals, makes the art of filmmaking look easy, as it nails the fundamentals of narrative storytelling with ease. The moment that even the stuffiest Oscar voters had to put their hands up and give Tommy Lee Jones the statuette had to have been the "I don't care" scene in the storm drain, as the Men in Black actor delivered the fury of a Shakespeare monologue in just three one-syllable words. There's something so undeniable about Jones' conviction as his character faces a crossroads. A desperate Kimble could feasibly pull the trigger, and Gerard shows fear, but he never lets it interfere with his devout commitment to his job.

Speaking to the movie's timeless nature, "I don't care" is a moment that could have emerged in a Warner Bros. thriller from the 1940s. The brevity of the line is not its only admirable feat, as Tommy Lee Jones' signature moment in The Fugitive crystallizes the dramatic weight of the film. Andrew Davis' enduring thriller is devoid of themes and subtext in the traditional sense because it's a film about characters defined by their actions. Samuel Gerard has nothing of deep substance to say to Kimble during this pivotal moment. He just wants to bring this man into custody. When you're stuck in a grave misunderstanding, arguing with someone defined by their profession is an impossible mountain to climb.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 brought several new features to the Messages app, including a setting that’s long been a popular request: the ability to customize or turn off the audio button. Here’s how to use it.

With iOS 27, Apple fixed a lot of bugs and also granted many feature requests from over the years.

Recent findings suggest that siri AI is the biggest example of that, offering a substantial upgrade over the old Siri. But smaller changes in apps like Calendar, Mail, and Messages reflect this focus on wish fulfillment.

In Messages, there’s a latest setting that I instantly starting using. It lets you turn off the audio button that normally lives on the right side of the text input field.

The audio button has been conveniently accessible there for years, but I never use it. I don’t think I’ve ever sent an audio message. Sometimes I use dictation, but that’s always available from the bottom-right of the keyboard.

It has been revealed that since I never need that button, the only time it gets pressed is by accident. And as I suspect a lot of customers have encountered—including Justin Bieber—it’s very easy to hit by accident.

Thankfully, iOS 27 has the fix. To disable the audio button, follow these steps:.

Even if you turn the audio button off, you can still send audio messages by hitting the + button to open your iMessage apps then selecting ‘Audio.’.

If you prefer to keep the button active, you can alternately now select ‘Record Audio’ or ‘Start Dictation’ as its function. That way the button will always stay set to your preference instead of dynamically changing like it did before.

Will you disable the audio button in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

  • Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-newly introduced iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

The iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

Industry observers note that the iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

In a recent development, the iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

It has been revealed that the biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

Industry observers note that the iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Recent findings suggest that contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

Recent findings suggest that for most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

It has been revealed that the iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

Recent findings suggest that black Friday is here and that means it's time to save big on bingeing the best shows and movies. Many of the best streaming services have slashed prices to their lowest of the year (and some are the lowest of all time).

Right now you can save 79% on some of the most popular platforms. My favorite Black Friday streaming service deal is the Disney+/Hulu bundle at $4.99/month (was $11.99). Other great deals include HBO Max for $5.49/month for 12 months and Paramount+ Premium for $2.99.

I'm digging through all the best Black Friday streaming deals, so you can enjoy a huge wealth of content without crushing your wallet that's probably already strained around the holidays.

According to recent reports, the Disney+ and Hulu bundle is a solid savings all year long, but for Black Friday, it's an even bigger bargain at $4.99. For less than $5 a month, you get two streaming services, offering the best of Disney, Marvel and Star Wars, alongside Hulu's excellent library of more grown-up content. Even better, if you lock in this discounted price today, you'll get Disney+ and Hulu at almost 60% off for a full 12 months.

Sources indicate that paramount+ has discounted every tier to $2.99, so the choice is obvious: get Paramount+ Premium. With this top-tier package, you get full access to the Paramount+ library with ad-free streaming, Showtime originals, and your local CBS station. There's plenty to watch, from the final season of "Yellowjackets" to live sports, like NFL and Champions League soccer. The only downside is that this offer is only valid for 2 months, which feels stingy compared to rivals.

Apple TV is a streaming service you shouldn't overlook. It packs one of the best original libraries of any streamer, with a wealth of must-watch TV demonstrates you can't find anywhere else. Ahead of Black Friday, Apple TV is 50% off, giving you six months of access for $6.99 a month. That's enough time to binge a wide selection of the very best Apple TV Originals from "Severance" to "Slow Horses".

HBO Max is offering 50% off its Basic with Ads plan. Half price on our favorite streaming service is a deal we're eager to shout about. HBO Max offers a near-unbeatable library with top-tier television and plenty of blockbuster movies. Sweetening the deal, the discounted price lasts for 12 months, so you can stream the best of HBO Max for an entire year. Get it now ahead of "Harry Potter" season 1 arriving in December.

Recent findings suggest that peacock skipped Black Friday last year, but has returned with a respectable discount for 2026. It's not the most headline-grabbing saving at 31%, but plans start from $2.99 per month for the Select tier. However, I recommend the Premium tier for $8.99, which gives you access to the full Peacock library, including indicates, movies, live sports, and Peacock Originals.

Sources indicate that horror fans, this one's worth a look. You can at the moment add MGM+ to your Prime Video subscription for just $1.99 per month for two months, down from $7.99, saving 75%. It's home to brilliant originals like "From" and "The Institute," plus a great selection of movies, including "Project Hail Mary.".

In a recent development, prime Video add-on subscriptions: deals from $0.99Prime Video add-on subscriptions offer some of the cheapest Black Friday streaming deals of the season. Discounts start from $0.99 and include Paramount+, Apple TV, HBO Max, Starz, AMC+, MGM+, BritBox and Hallmark+. Upgrade your Prime Video library with these great deals.

Starz add-on subscription via Prime Video (3 months): was $11.99/month now $2.99/month @ AmazonThe Starz add-on is worth it on Prime Video if you want consistently bingeable shows and great movies without hunting around. You get sweeping dramas like "Outlander," the endlessly addictive "Power" universe, and on the movie side, there are recent favorites including "The Housemaid" and "Shelter." You'll need to clear your summer schedule to watch everything that Starz has to offer.

Sources indicate that if you're a fan of British TV and don't normally have access to it, a BritBox subscription might be for you. Right now, you can jump in and try it for $2.99 a month for the first two months. You'll get "Downton Abbey," "Death In Paradise," "Vera," "Father Brown", "Ludwig" and many more.
